flags.headline: Copper-tariff-plan stall plus record-high reversal drive a direct hit to the copper-cyclicality thesis risk
flags.detail: New today. FCX fell 6.58% to $71.21 after Reuters reported (via multiple syndicated outlets) that the White House's refined-copper tariff plan has stalled amid affordability concerns ahead of the November midterms, removing a key support for the record copper rally. Copper itself touched an all-time intraday high (~$14,875/tonne) before reversing hard, ending five straight sessions of gains. Rising Treasury yields and broad industrial-metals profit-taking amplified the move. This is a direct, tier-1-confirmed materialization of FCX's own listed key_risk on copper-price cyclicality.
flags.thesis_link: Matches FCX key_risk: 'Copper price cyclicality -- a correction from current $5.50+/lb to $3.50/lb would slash EBITDA by 40%+ and stress the $4.3-4.5B annual capex program, as profit margin of 8.5% provides thin cushion against commodity downturns.'

evidence.source: Reuters (via Investing.com) -- 'White House copper tariff plan stalls amid affordability concerns, sources say'
Seeking Alpha -- 'Copper stocks slump as White House tariff plan reportedly stalls (FCX:NYSE)'

flags.headline: Holding worsens further after CFO-disclosed manufacturing constraints, no resolution
flags.detail: First flagged 2026-09-09 after Stryker CFO Preston Wells (Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference, Sept 8) disclosed peripheral-vascular manufacturing constraints tied to the company's earlier cyber incident, expected to persist into Q4 2026 and drag organic growth 70-80bps for a third straight quarter, plus a softer joint-replacement (hip) environment. Shares are down a further 2.0% today to $270.01 (from the post-disclosure 52-week low of $276.43) -- no fresh news, but no sign of resolution either; full-year guidance (8.3-9.3%) is unchanged. Separately, a Sept 8 'SYK ALERT' press release announcing a securities-fraud investigation by a plaintiff law firm (Block & Leviton) is standard post-selloff solicitation, not a tier-1-confirmed development, and is noted here only so it isn't mistaken for new information. Not one of SYK's three listed key_risks (valuation/margin-of-safety, profit-margin ceiling, hospital-capex sensitivity) -- still worth adding as a fourth, newly-materialized risk at the next screener refresh.

flags.headline: US-Iran conflict escalates further -- Iran fires a ballistic missile at a US warship near the Strait of Hormuz
flags.detail: First flagged 2026-09-06; escalates further this run. The monthlong lull broke in early September and has continued deteriorating: in the past 24h the US struck three Iranian oil tankers and Iran struck tankers and fired a ballistic missile toward US warships patrolling near the strait. Brent has climbed above $105/bbl (from the high-$80s/low-$90s range earlier in this conflict), and August PPI (released 9/10) showed a 4.2% surge in energy costs directly attributed to the conflict. Despite the escalation, today's energy-sleeve price reaction is muted rather than directional -- DVN +2.11% ($50.02), VLO -0.91%, CVX -0.47%, OKE -0.15%, CNX -0.20% -- consistent with a market that has already priced in an elevated-and-volatile oil complex rather than reacting fresh to each headline. Held at RED given the unresolved, intensifying military conflict and DVN's direct oil-price-volatility key_risk exposure.
flags.thesis_link: Matches DVN key_risk: 'Oil and gas price volatility remains the dominant swing factor for earnings and free cash flow ... could reverse quickly given global supply dynamics.'
